title: The messengers arrived at Lut's door.
subtitle: The same angels, now in a different town

row.title: Lut's family
sub: one house in a guilty town

then: The scene moves from Ibrahim's house to Lut's. Ibn Kathir says {idea}the angels came to Lut in the form of young men with handsome faces{/idea}. Nobody in town knew who had just walked in.
now: Some days look like every other day: a knock on the door, a call, a stranger at the bus stop. {idea}You rarely know which ordinary moment is carrying something big.{/idea} That is a reason to treat each one well.
old: Nothing important happens on a normal day.
new: Allah's decree often arrives looking ordinary, through a door like any other.
try: Treat the next person who knocks, calls or asks for help today as if the moment matters.

title: Lut did not recognize who they were.
subtitle: You are people unknown to me
then: When the guests entered, Lut said {idea}you are people unknown to me{/idea}. He knew how dangerous his town was for strangers. He did not yet know they were angels, or what they carried.
now: Something new walks into your life: a diagnosis, a move, a person. You feel uneasy because you cannot place it. {idea}Lut did not understand either, at first.{/idea} The meaning came a moment later.
old: If I cannot make sense of this right now, something is wrong.
new: Even a prophet did not see the meaning at first; understanding can come a step later.
try: When something unclear happens today, say: O Allah, show me the good in this, and wait.

title: What they doubted for years was at the door.
subtitle: The thing they kept disputing
then: The angels said {trap}we have come to you with that which they were doubting{/trap}. Ibn Kathir explains they were bringing the punishment the people doubted they would ever suffer. Makkah too had been mocking the warning for years.
now: You keep putting off the check-up, the debt plan, the talk with your son, telling yourself it is not that serious. {trap}Doubting a consequence does not delay it.{/trap} {idea}Better to act while it is still a warning.{/idea}
old: If I do not think about it, it will not come.
new: What I doubt or ignore still arrives; my doubt changes only how ready I am.
try: Take one step today on something you have been avoiding because it feels scary.

title: Truth came, and the messengers said it plainly.
subtitle: We have brought the truth, and we are truthful
then: Ibn Kathir links this to 15:8: {idea}We do not send the angels down except with the truth{/idea}. Earlier in this surah, Makkah had demanded angels as proof. Here is what angels look like when they come: {trap}a decree, not a show{/trap}.
now: You keep asking for a sign before you change: a dream, a miracle, a perfect moment. {idea}When the real sign comes, it comes with consequences already attached.{/idea} It is kinder to act on the message you already have.
old: If Allah wanted me to change, He would send me a clear sign.
new: The signs I already have are mercy; a final sign arrives carrying the outcome.
try: Act today on one piece of guidance you already know, without waiting for a sign.

title: Walk behind your family, and do not look back.
subtitle: Leaving at night, with eyes forward
then: The angels told Lut to leave in part of the night and walk behind his family to protect them. Ibn Kathir says {idea}the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would walk in the rear of the army to help the weak{/idea}. And {trap}no one was to turn back{/trap} toward the town.
now: The family is moving cities, or leaving a bad situation. You are the one who makes sure the youngest is not left behind, and you stop scrolling the old life's photos. {idea}Protect the people with you. Keep walking.{/idea}
old: A leader goes first and gets out first.
new: The one in charge walks at the back, guarding the weak, and keeps eyes forward.
try: Today, be the last one to leave a gathering, making sure everyone is home or helped.

title: He was told the hour before the town knew.
subtitle: The end would come by early morning
then: Allah {idea}made this decree known to him{/idea}: they would be rooted out in the early morning. Ibn Kathir quotes 11:81, {trap}morning is their appointed time; is not the morning near?{/trap}
now: You plan to fix things with Allah later: after the exams, after the wedding, after retirement. {trap}Morning is always nearer than it feels at night.{/trap} {idea}Today is a good time.{/idea}
old: I have plenty of time before any of this matters.
new: The appointed time is closer than it feels; morning is always near.
try: Do tonight the one good thing you keep saying you will do someday.

title: They came rejoicing at the chance to do wrong.
subtitle: The people of the city hear about the guests

key.label: When sin feels like good news

then: Ibn Kathir says the people {trap}came to Lut when they found out about his guests, happily rejoicing{/trap}. They meant harm, and were glad about it. They had no idea the morning would bring their end.
now: You hear a juicy rumor about a colleague and feel a little thrill. The chance to cut a corner unseen feels like luck. {trap}When wrongdoing starts to feel like good news, something inside has shifted.{/trap}
old: Feeling excited about something means it is good for me.
new: Being happy at a chance to do wrong is a sign to stop, not a green light.
try: Notice one moment today where a wrong choice feels exciting, and walk away from it.

title: These are my guests; do not shame me.
subtitle: Lut stands between the crowd and his guests
then: Lut said, {idea}these are my guests, so do not shame me{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says he said this before he knew they were angels. He thought they were ordinary young men, and still {idea}he stood up for them{/idea}.
now: Your guest at the family gathering is being mocked by a cousin. A new hire is being picked on in the group chat. {idea}You are the host here.{/idea} Their dignity is tied to yours.
old: It is not my place to defend someone else.
new: When someone is under my roof or my care, protecting their dignity is my duty.
try: Stand up, gently, for one person today who is being talked down to near you.

title: He reminded a mob to fear Allah.
subtitle: Appealing to conscience in the worst moment
then: Facing the crowd alone, Lut said {idea}have taqwa of Allah, and do not disgrace me{/idea}. He did not have power, so he spoke to their conscience. Ibn Kathir notes this was before he knew his guests were angels.
now: Your friends are about to do something cruel to someone online. You are one voice. {idea}Saying come on, fear Allah, this is not right{/idea} might feel useless. It is still the right thing to say.
old: If I cannot stop it, there is no point saying anything.
new: Even when outnumbered, reminding people of Allah is a real act, whether or not they listen.
try: If you see wrong today, say one calm sentence against it, even if it changes nothing.

title: They had already banned him from protecting anyone.
subtitle: A town that punished kindness
then: They answered him: {trap}did we not forbid you from protecting people?{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains they meant, did we not tell you not to have anyone as a guest? The town had turned hospitality itself into an offense.
now: At work, the one who reports the problem gets sidelined. At school, the kid who defends the bullied one gets bullied too. {trap}When doing good gets you in trouble, the place is upside down.{/trap} {idea}Keep doing it anyway.{/idea}
old: If people tell me to stop helping, maybe I should.
new: When kindness itself is punished, the problem is the place, not the kindness.
try: Do one quiet kindness today for someone others avoid.

title: He pointed them to what Allah had made lawful.
subtitle: Lut's last appeal: these are my daughters

row.title: lawful marriage
sub: with the women of their people

then: Lut said, {idea}these are my daughters, if you would be doers{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains he reminded them about their womenfolk and {idea}what their Lord had created for them in lawful relationships{/idea}. All this while they did not know the morning would bring their end.
now: A desire pulls you somewhere you know is wrong, and it feels like the only option. {idea}Allah almost always leaves a lawful door open beside the forbidden one.{/idea} Look for it before you give in.
old: There is no way to meet this need without crossing a line.
new: Allah has already provided a lawful path; the forbidden one is never the only door.
try: Name one temptation you struggle with and identify its lawful alternative today.

title: Drunk on their wrong, they wandered blind.
subtitle: An oath by the Prophet's life
then: Allah {idea}swore by the life of His Prophet ﷺ{/idea}. Ibn Abbas said he never heard that Allah swore by the life of anyone else. Qatadah said intoxication here means {trap}their misguided state, and they were playing{/trap}, blind to what was coming.
now: You are deep in something: a feud, a binge, a scheme, a screen at two in the morning. Everyone else can see where it is going. {trap}You cannot.{/trap} {idea}Sin works like that. It blurs the road ahead.{/idea}
old: I know exactly what I am doing.
new: Wrongdoing can make a person blind to where they are heading, like being drunk.
try: Ask one trusted person today: is there anything in my life you think I am blind to?

title: At sunrise, the shout came.
subtitle: The morning they never expected
then: Ibn Kathir describes the Sayhah as {trap}the piercing sound that came to them when the sun rose{/trap}. It was the morning Lut had been told about. The night before, they were still celebrating.
now: People say I will change when I see it coming. Endings rarely announce themselves. The call from the hospital, the layoff email, the last conversation. {idea}Live tonight as if the morning matters.{/idea}
old: I will get a clear warning before anything serious happens.
new: The decisive moment can arrive suddenly, on an ordinary morning.
try: Before you sleep tonight, forgive someone and make your peace with Allah.

title: The top of their town became the bottom.
subtitle: A city turned upside down
then: Ibn Kathir says the sound came with {trap}the city being flipped upside down, and stones of baked clay raining down{/trap}. He calls Sodom a city {idea}physically and spiritually turned upside down{/idea}. They had already inverted right and wrong.
now: Look at the small places where you call wrong right: the white lie that is just being polite, the gossip that is just venting. {idea}Turning values upside down starts small.{/idea} You can turn yours the right way up today.
old: Bending right and wrong a little is harmless.
new: When people flip right and wrong, the result can turn their whole world over.
try: Pick one wrong you have been calling by a softer name, and call it what it is.

title: Signs for those who look closely.
subtitle: The ones with insight
then: Ibn Kathir says the traces are visible to anyone who ponders, {idea}with physical eyesight or mental and spiritual insight{/idea}. Mujahid said those who discern means {idea}those who have insight and discernment{/idea}; Qatadah said those who learn lessons.
now: You watch a documentary about a collapsed empire, or drive past a closed factory that once employed your whole town. {idea}Most people see buildings. A discerning person sees a lesson.{/idea}
old: History is just what happened to other people.
new: The traces of past peoples are signs for whoever looks with insight.
try: Next time you pass a ruin or an abandoned place, pause and ask what it teaches you.

title: The ruins sit on a road people still travel.
subtitle: The lesson was never hidden
then: Ibn Kathir says Sodom {idea}is on a route that is easily accessible until the present day{/idea}. The trade caravans of Makkah passed it. He cites 37:137-138: {idea}you pass by them morning and night; will you not reflect?{/idea}
now: The same road you drive to work passes a cemetery. The same feed you scroll shows stories of people ruined by the same habits you have. {idea}The lessons are on your daily route.{/idea}
old: If there were a lesson for me, I would have noticed it.
new: Lessons are placed on the roads I already travel; noticing them is up to me.
try: On your commute today, look for one sign along the way and reflect on it for a minute.

title: Rescue and ruin, both a sign for believers.
subtitle: The whole story of Lut as one lesson
then: Ibn Kathir sums it up: {idea}all We did to the people of Lut, from the destruction, to how We saved Lut and his family{/idea}, are clear signs to those who believe. For the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah, it meant {reward}the faithful are not forgotten{/reward}.
now: You feel like the only one trying to do right at work or at home. This story ends with {reward}one small family walked out to safety{/reward}. {idea}Allah sees the few who stay upright.{/idea}
old: Stories of punishment are just meant to scare me.
new: The story shows both justice and rescue; the believer takes hope as well as warning.
try: Make dua tonight: O Allah, make me and my family among those You save.
